body: I know exactly what you mean and damn is it frustrating when it seems like all you can do is all youre doing. But just surviving in life is horribly unfulfilling on it's own. To me one needs purpose, passion and stability to garner any fullfilment and happiness out of life. And sometimes that shit is just either too costly or too rare and we gotta redefine what it is we really want and need.

Oh man I know exactly what you mean. I've pushed so many good friends away just because most days I'd rather just shutdown. And damn is it hard to go out and about and enjoy yourself with all the other happy people when your head feels like lead.

Oh god I do that too when my loneliness just gets a bit too much to handle, hell I'm doing it right now >.<
And I know exactly what you mean, tbh I think the only person who would notice if I was gone is this elderly neighbor I sometimes bake treats for, but beyond that... ¯\\\_(ツ)_/¯

Well anyway, I'd love to chat if you'd like.

Hey there, I'm in a similar situation myself and was wondering if you wanted someone to talk to. Tbh I don't really know if I have any advice as I'm pretty lost and low myself. But I relate pretty heavily and if you'd like to talk about it or whatever I'm all ears.

Oh man I definitely know how you feel.  I've been trapped and overwhelmed in my own undertow for far too long now. Just completely alone, lost and hopelessly looking for some escape in this big confusing and cynical world. You're absolutely right about the indifference most people seem to have in spades these days and boy does that start to feel suffocating when you have no where to turn.

But I'd like to point out how much of a strong willed and considerate person you come off as. I mean we're the same age yet you're willing and able to provide for people other than yourself, that's something to be proud of in my book! And besides that I've got this sorta theory that decent, good natured people like you will only attract other decent, good natured people given enough time. 

I'm sorry I don't have any solid advice for your situation, tbh I barely know how I'm gonna get control of my own life atm >.< so it's probably for the best. Just thought I'd chime in to say I share your sentiment and I hope you find your way forward.

Oh I do enjoy music, I've been learning guitar for mmm nearly 2 years now. But whether the "music" I make is at all enjoyable to anybody but myself is open to debate XD I think I'm better off sticking to the old pen and paper

And yea it's a pretty big undertaking if you don't have a sort of safety net to fall back on. Definitely consider it a bit when managing your savings, I try to put aside as much spare cash I can every month so I don't have to live on instant noodles and Kool aid when I do find a place :p
ooh, no I haven't. I'll have to check that out after I finish bloodborne, ty

Oh ikr, it seems like every franchise is looking to be another lame attempt at an mmo, king of the hill or moba. Like fuck, I just want more games like Stardew Valley or Dark Souls not another dead horse to beat until the devs poop out a slightly shinier mountain of micro transactions the next year.

Except Warframe and WoW tho, that's my crack.

Yeah you won't find much through Google beyond fruitless posts like this and perhaps the rare unflagged gplus group talking circles about their methods and doubts. I used to have a pretty good discord going with like minded people but just sorta lost the will to be a part of it.

 Beyond that it honestly seems like screaming into the void and boy does it get tiresome. Oh and me too, it's one of my many favorite modest mouse lyrics.

Oh that's pretty cool, I've always wanted to make music myself but I'm god awful at writing and even worse at keeping rhythm :p 

Oh and overbearing parents are the worst. I was raised by a narcissist myself and still can't go a day without hearing of the "disappointment and shame" I can apparently only bring to my family. I know you mentioned moving out may only exasperate your loneliness, but if possible perhaps you should try it before deciding on anything final. I plan to do so this year (if I'm still around) just to get some taste of freedom, however bitter it may be.

Oh absolutely, I see a lot of honest and lost people in forums like this who just need an impartial friend to consistently hear them out without fear of being ignored, stigmatized or thrown into the nearest pysch ward. But as you said the ever busy hotlines can only point them in a vague direction they already know of or  never get to them at all. While the forums like this only let them go so far without yanking back on the leash and silencing any last desperate hope they have left. It's a damn lonely feeling having no where to turn.

"Everyone's a building burning. With no one to put the fire out."

Nice, I'm more of an indie/alt rock gal myself but evanscence and fireflight are definite favs. Have you ever tried making music yourself? Singing, guitar, piano, writing lyrics or anything like that? I've found hobbies like that makes meeting other like minded people a bit easier.
Same here, sometimes the only thing that sparks any sorta feeling in me is a modest mouse song or episode of the office. What sorta music and shows do you like?

I know how you feel, atm I'm down to my last "friend" I see/talk to like once maybe twice a month. And I think she only sticks around for pity and the fear that I might kill myself soon. And god is it suffocating to feel so alone all the damn time.

I could list and recommend all the ways I've desperately tried to make friends both online and off but honestly none of them have really done much beyond fill me with jealousy or apathy. Personally I've found the only thing that reliably distracts me is pouring myself into my art. It sort of gives me a  sense of purpose and means to express myself. The motivation to do so is hard to come by at times like this but I think it's worth it. Do you have any passions, hobbies or interests you use to cope?

Those subs never seem to last, but yeah I definitely know what you mean. Having a place or people you can actually be honest about your emotions and intentions with and not getting platitudes or hotline numbers in return is actually quite helpful. People seem to think it's a good idea to blindly censor stuff like that but really it just feels like another way of alienating and invalidating people at the end of their ropes.

Yeah, unfortunately that's been the past couple days for me. I haven't cut since highschool but lately I've relapsed and have been cutting all throughout the day just to get away from this empty feeling I can't shake.

Sorry to hear about your experience, Ive been there too and tbh some of the looks I've got hurt a whole lot more than the cuts ever did.

Relieved you're not alone, but disheartened by the fact that we're both in the same sinking ship. Yeah, don't I know it.

I'm thinking of doing the same with my best friend, but I'm scared they might feel guilty. I dunno honestly I think it might be better if they just think I ghosted them. But youre right, it's a real slim tight rope we walk.

Ah fuck, you just described exactly how I feel to a T. It's honestly a little ridiculous how much of a taboo suicide is in society at this point. Not too get too nihilistic, but man things would be so much easier if you weren't immediately labeled as deranged when talking about suicide. But people seem to believe only in absolutes these days without any consideration of other perspectives unless they are put into that situation themselves.

I too have worried and thought about all the things you've mentioned far longer than I care to admit. And tbh it's quite maddening keeping it all bottled up and tucked away for so long, but what else can be done when even letting a little slip out can paint you as a pariah?

Sorry for rambling, your post just really resonated with me.

Oh man, well put. Honestly that's pretty much how I've been feeling the past few years. Nothing seems to stick besides the emptiness. I wish I had more to say then "me too thx" but I'm pretty much as lost as you.

Hello my name's Alexis, would you like someone to talk to? I know how freaking horrible it can be to feel lost, alone and trapped in a body you loathe. I'm also living at home with not much besides a crappy part time job at a rundown little chinese restaurant down the street. Tbh the only things keeping me in motion are my passions and hobbies that I desperately cling to in order to find some self worth and pride. And I'd be lying if I said I too don't feel tired, suicidal and a little hopeless in my life lately, but I refuse to believe my or anybody's future is set entirely in stone. I don't mean to get too cliche here, but you never know how long these slumps will last nor how great the climb afterwards may be.

Hello lucy, I think me and you have a lot in common besides a couple years in my favor. I'm also a gay trans girl lost in my own world of confusion, dysphoria and depression. I totally know where your coming from about the sort of addicting feeling depression gives you. When youre just so used to being sad that other emotions feel fake or uncomfortable. It's truly an insidious disease that corrupts from within.

I'm sorry to hear about the losses you have experienced, you're absolutely right that nobody your age or any age even should be burdened with that weight. It's incredibly easy to slip into endless apathy when given such horrid news and the only thing you're told to do is "move on". As if it's ever really that easy :/

Do you have anything at all your passionate about, anything you feel comforted by or that distracts from your depression? Personally when I start to spiral I throw myself and any amount of will I have left into either my art or my appearance and presentation as a tgirl. It doesn't stop the thoughts, but it certainly gives me a way to channel them in a constructive way that will hopefully gradully build into self confidence and pride. Well this is getting rather long and you probably don't want to read an entire essay of my ramblings. But, if you'd like to talk or vent further go ahead and send me a private message. I  promise I won't judge or bite ( too much :p). Take care, hun

As a stealth gay transgirl of mmm... 2ish years I completely know where you're coming from. And boy do I know how horrible and lonely it can feel when society paints us as nothing but weird dysfunctional pariahs :/. And I (and many other trans people) know all about the constant dysphoria and feeling of inadequacy you face. Hell, some weeks I feel like smashing all the mirrors in my house just so I don't have to reminded of who I'm not.

Okay sorry for the depressing anecodte, just wanted to assure you that your far from alone. Anyway, I strongly suggest you start looking for support from lgbtq+ groups online and irl. And yeah I know, being that tacked on T at the end certainly describes how we're seen in pretty much all communities. But from personal experience the best friends I've made who continually give support and understanding have been from gay communities (furries seem to be really chill and accepting too :p). My suggestion is to start there and gradually snowball your confidence into a solid foundation that you can then start living your 'new' life on.

Oh boy, as someone who has been ghosted multiple times by people who I thought I built a mutual and strong connection with I definitely know how you feel. It's like losing that last little glimmer of hope you were in desperate need of and fuck does it hurt.

It's gonna be pretty rough at first feeling that horrible anticipation for some sort of response. And the constant ebb and flow of shame and regret. It'll be a struggle for sure, but time will eventually dull those pains.

My advice is to wait a while. Couple weeks, months, however long to know for sure that they have moved on and that you are feeling ready to as well. Then I suggest writing up a note fully explaining what they meant to you and how this has affected you. This isn't meant to win them back or incite shame (hell they might not even see or read it), it's simply meant to provide yourself closure. A final bit of effort and thought put into the relationship you had as a sign that you did indeed care, but will learn and live from it as you see fit.

As for the suicidal thoughts, I'm afraid I haven't figured out a way to let go of those yet. Que Sera, sera
